topics.title: Leona Helmsley Discusses Hale House and Jealousy
topics.summary: During a radio interview, Leona Helmsley discusses her visit to Hale House where she discussed decorating choices with residents. She attributes negative feelings towards herself as stemming from jealousy among others regarding her wealth and status, while briefly referencing legal issues involving tax evasion.

topics.title: Child Support, Hollywood Squares & Carly Simon
topics.summary: During an interview, a man discusses receiving child support from Conrad Hilton and recounts meeting Carly Simon at Hollywood Squares, describing her as attractive while discussing his television production work in London and Rome. He shares anecdotes about writing children’s books and encounters with other celebrities like Jim J. Bullock.

topics.title: Kids’ Book Secrets & Boxing Dreams – Naked Beach
topics.summary: A man discusses his children’s book ideas, including a ‘Bubble Monster,’ a dog in bed, and an incident on a beach with naked people while discussing boxing with a guest who claims to be a professional fighter. He then delves into multiple marriages, financial success, and the temptations of fame.

topics.title: Joe Frazier Discusses Stallone Screen Test & Racial Concerns
topics.summary: During a conversation, Joe Frazier recounts his frustration with Sylvester Stallone attempting to incorporate him into Rocky II, expressing concerns about ideas theft and racial appropriation in the entertainment industry. He details offers for screen tests and highlights potential similarities between his experiences and those of other Black artists.

topics.title: Blow Meat & Baltimore Blues – A Rambling Radio Session
topics.summary: During a chaotic radio interview, hosts discuss bizarre topics including ‘blow meat’ (marijuana), navigating dating while single, and confusing family names referencing car models. Tyrone Frazier uses the name 'John Mahatma Brim,' referencing his father's vehicle, leading to humorous misunderstandings and tangents about personal anecdotes.

topics.title: Family History & Commercial Break
topics.summary: Joe recounts his large family history – thirteen children including six girls and seven boys – detailing unusual naming conventions and challenges of raising so many kids. The segment concludes with a commercial for gas heat and Broadway tickets, featuring offers and an attempt to engage the listener.

topics.title: Man Draws, Discusses Family Beliefs
topics.summary: A man draws images on the ground and discusses his beliefs about human creation myths and mirroring others’ appearances. He recounts stories of a child learning language – ‘daddy’ – referencing origins and personal relationships, suggesting women are drawn to men's power while responsibility rests with the man.

topics.title: Security Guard Confrontation at Press Conference
topics.summary: During a press conference featuring Howard Stern and Paul McCartney, security repeatedly attempted to remove an unidentified man due to his unusual appearance and disruptive behavior. The incident involved heated exchanges questioning the guard’s actions, with multiple individuals expressing disbelief about the man's attire and conduct, culminating in accusations of discrimination.

topics.title: IRS Deduction & The Lonely Mayor
topics.summary: A caller details a business deduction with the IRS, followed by an increasingly bizarre monologue about planning a New Year’s party for a solitary ex-mayor. He lists eccentric guests like ‘Homo no mo,’ Gracie Mansion and attempts to flirt inappropriately while discussing vague references and ultimately confusing concepts.

topics.title: Personal Reflections on Sexuality and Comedy
topics.summary: The conversation centers around personal experiences, including discussions of sexual language and its perceived offensiveness. Participants share anecdotes about their lives – long-term marriage, career choices in comedy and film, occasional drug use, and encounters with figures like Jackie Mason. They explore the challenges faced by comedians seeking recognition alongside reflections on social norms regarding taboo subjects.
